title: You’ve read past his name before.
paragraphs: You’ve read past his name before.
Quickly. Casually. Like it didn’t matter.
Tucked between greetings and closing lines… almost invisible.
And if you’re paying attention—neither should you.
And his story is only one sentence long.
One sentence… that exposes something most believers are trying to ignore.
You know that feeling when something God told you to do keeps coming back?
The church in Colossae was alive. People were growing. Faith was spreading.
Then in the middle of a letter, almost like an interruption, comes this line:
“Tell Archippus: ‘See to it that you complete the ministry you have received in the Lord.’” — Colossians 4:17
Which means he had already begun.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
God doesn’t remind you to finish something unless you’ve stopped.
We don’t know what Archippus’ assignment was.
Because this isn’t just about him.
That thing God placed in your hands—
Just enough to ease your conscience.
You still talk like you’re called.
But you’re no longer walking like you are.
This is where most people drift into a dangerous place.
Jesus told a parable that cuts deeper than most want to admit:
“No one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.” — Luke 9:62
You don’t start with Christ and then slowly negotiate your way out of obedience.
And here’s the tension most people avoid:
But before shame tries to take over…
The same God who corrected Archippus didn’t discard him.
Because the Gospel is not just about being saved from sin…
It’s about being restored to purpose.
“For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand, that we should walk in them.” — Ephesians 2:10
You were not saved to sit still.
You were not rescued to remain passive.
There is something God assigned to you.
And Jesus didn’t just die to forgive your failure.
He died to empower your obedience.
So you would have no excuse to abandon yours.
Where conviction fades into background noise.
Where you stand before God with explanations instead of obedience.
Where you pick it back up.
Where obedience costs you something—but produces eternal weight.
If something inside you just tightened…
Don’t bury it like the last time.
Say it if you feel it:
“I will finish what God started in me.”
There are people tied to your obedience.
There are souls connected to your “yes.”
There are things God wants to do through you that will never happen if you keep delaying.
Stay under truth that corrects you, not comforts your excuses.
Grow where you are stretched, not where you are entertained.
Follow here if you’re done playing surface-level faith.
And if you know someone who started strong but quietly drifted…
Because you will feel tempted again.
And when you do—this moment matters.
